media.title: Flag of Israel.svg
media.artist:
Israel Belkind and Fanny Abramovitch (original)
“The Provisional Council of State Proclamation of the Flag of the State of Israel” of 25 Tishrei 5709 (28 October 1948) provides the official specification for the design of the Israeli flag.
The color of the Magen David and the stripes of the Israeli flag is not precisely specified by the above legislation.  The color depicted in the current version of the image is typical of flags used in Israel today, although individual flags can and do vary.
The flag legislation officially specifies dimensions of 220 cm × 160 cm.  However, the sizes of actual flags vary (although the aspect ratio is usually retained).
media.credit: Own work using: http://mfa.gov.il/MFA/AboutIsrael/IsraelAt50/Pages/The%20Flag%20and%20the%20Emblem.aspx

media.title: Royal Standard of the King of France.svg
media.credit:
Own work based on:




“

Pavillon royal de France.
il est blanc semé de fleurs de lis d’or, chargé des armes de France, entouré des colliers des ordres de S. Michel & du S. Esprit, & deux anges pour support.


”


—Encyclopédie, ou Dictionnaire raisonné des sciences, des arts et des métiers (1751).




“

Pavillon Roïal de France.
il est blanc, semé de fleurs de lis d'or, & chargé d'un Écusson des armes de France, entouré des Colliers des ordres de St Michel & du St Esprit.


”


—La connoissance des pavillons ou bannieres que la plûpart des nations arborent en mer (1737). A depiction of 'Pavillon Royal De France' is shown in the same book.




		
			
			the standard flying from a first rate Admiral's flagship (painted 1693)
		
		
			
			The standard flying from the Soleil-Royal at the Battle of Barleur (painted 1693 by Ludolf Bakhuizen)
		
		
			
			'Pavillons de France' from 'Le Neptune françois, ou Atlas nouveau des cartes marines' (P. Mortier, 1700).
		
		
			
			Image of the 'Pavillon royal de France' from the 'Encyclopédie, ou Dictionnaire raisonné des sciences' (1751).
		
		
			
			White flag of France with the fleur-de-lis of the Bourbon kings, flanked by two angels. (Flags through the ages and cross the world 1975 by Whitney Smith.)

media.title: Flag of Morocco.svg
media.credit:
Moroccan royal decree (17 November 1915), BO-135_ar page 6 (Arabic) - BO-162_fr page 6 (French)


		
			
			Arabic-language text
		
		
			
			French-language text
		

English Translation: Cherifian Dahir concerning the distinction of the Moroccan flag — Let it be known from this Our noble decree, may God exalt its value and make happiness and prosperity revolve around its center, that, in view of the advancement of the affairs of Our Cherifian Kingdom, the spread of its glory and renown, and the circumstances requiring that it be distinguished by a flag setting it apart from other kingdoms; and whereas the flag of Our revered ancestors resembled certain other flags, particularly those used for maritime signals; Our noble consideration has decreed that Our blessed flag be distinguished by placing the five-pointed Seal of Solomon at its center, in green, beseeching Almighty God to keep it ever flying with the winds of fortune and prosperity, in the present and in the future. Amen and peace.
Moroccan royal decree (23 November 2005), BO-5378-ar page 5 (Arabic) - BO-5378-fr page 6 (French)

English Translation: Cherifian Dahir with reference 1.05.99 issued on 20 Shawwal 1426 (23 November 2005) concerning the characteristics of the Kingdom’s flag and national anthem — In accordance with Article Seven of the Constitution, the flag of the Kingdom shall be a red banner bearing a green five-pointed star at its center. The flag shall be made of vivid red fabric, opaque and rectangular in shape. The star shall be open, palm green in color, composed of five continuous points, and woven into the same fabric so as to be visible on both sides of the flag. One of its points shall be directed upward. The hoist (vertical dimension) of the flag shall be equal to two thirds (2/3) of its fly (horizontal length). The star shall be inscribed within an invisible circle whose radius is equal to one sixth (1/6) of the flag’s fly (horizontal length), the center of which coincides with the intersection of the invisible diagonal lines of the flag’s rectangle. The width of each branch of the star shall be equal to one twentieth (1/20) of its length.

media.title: Flag of Morocco (1666–1915).svg
media.credit:
Own work by uploader - 

EL, Noble Timothy Myers- (30 December 2004)    (in English)   The Huevolution of Sacred Muur Science Past and Present: A Theoretical Compilation, Author House  ISBN:  978-1-4184-6949-8. : "Interesting enough 1912 was the year the green 5-pointed star was put in the center of the all red Moroccan flag".
Minahan, James (2010)    (in English)   The Complete Guide to National Symbols and Emblems, Greenwood Press, pp. 617  ISBN:  978-0-313-34500-5. : "The flag of Morocco before 1915 was a plain red field".
(in English) (1907)  Railway Conductors' Monthly, pp. 631  : "In nation's index the red flag stand for Morocco, an Empire or Sultanate, in the northwestern part of Africa".
“Chapter 9. The First 'Red Flag'”, in The Half-Lives of Pat Lowther[1], University of Toronto Press, 2005-01-31, pages 134
"The Alawite dynasty first adopted a red flag for Morocco in the 17th century . Red symbolizes the royal family".
(in English)   The Report: Emerging Morocco 2007, Oxford Business Group, pp. 10  ISBN:  978-1-902339-76-4. : "FLAG: The Moroccan flag is red with a Solomon's seal, a five-pointed star outlined in green. The red flag was introduced by the Alaouite dynasty in the beginning of the 17th century. The Sulayman star was introduced in 1912 to distinguish the country's flag from others. Green and red are colours associated with Islam".
Bowen, Patrick D. (11 September 2017)    (in English)   A History of Conversion to Islam in the United States, Volume 2: The African American Islamic Renaissance, 1920-1975, BRILL, pp. 26  ISBN:  978-90-04-35437-1. : "It is worth noting, too, that in the late seventeenth century, Morocco's Muslim Alaouite dynasty adopted for its country's symbol the plain red flag, which had been used for hundreds of years by various Muslim communities, but was not at that time the symbol of another major African country".
Piquet, Victor (1918)    (in French)   Le Maroc: géographie--histoire--mise en valeur ..., A. Colin, pp. 263  : "The flag of the Sharifian Empire, which was completely red, has been, since the end of 1915, red with a green star in the shape of Solomon's ring".
(in French) (1906)  L'illustration, J. Dubochet, pp. 432  : "...l'étendard rouge - sang de l'empire chérifien".

		
			
			Moroccan flag in "British Library digitised image from page 337 of "Orient Line Guide"
		
		
			
			Moroccan flag in "Flags of the world 1911"
		
		
			
			Moroccan flag in "United States encyclopedia world flag chart published in 1904"

media.title: Flag of Namibia.svg
media.credit:
SVG implementation of the description in Schedule 6, Page 66 of the Constitution of Namibia. 
"The National Flag of Namibia shall be rectangular in the proportion of three in the length to two in the width, tierced per bend reversed, blue, white and green; the white bend reversed, which shall be one third of the width of the flag, is charged with another of red, one quarter of the width of the flag. In the upper hoist there shall be a gold sun with twelve straight rays, the diameter of which shall be one third of the width of the flag, with its vertical axis one fifth of the distance from the hoist, positioned equidistant from the top edge and from the reversed bend. The rays, which shall each be two fifths of the radius of the sun, issue from the outer edge of a blue ring, which shall be one tenth of the radius of the sun." Pantone from National Symbols of the Republic of Namibia Act, 2018, Schedule 4. "The colours of the Presidential Standard must be the same as that of the National Flag of Namibia, namely:
Pantone: 
Blue: 294c
Yellow (gold): 116c
Green: 347c

Red: 186c"

leaders.role: Kan de Mongolia · monarca bajo gobierno limitado

media.title: Flag of Sweden.svg
media.credit:
This flag is regulated by Swedish Law, Act 1970:498, which states that "in commercial activities, the coats of arms, the flag or other official insignia of Sweden may not be used in a trademark or other insignia for products or services without proper authorization. This includes any mark or text referring to the Swedish government which thus can give the commercial mark a sign of official endorsement. This includes municipal coats of arms which are registered."
Colors regulated by Ordinance (1983:826), which specifies the exact shades and their properties

media.title: Flag of Eritrea.svg
media.credit:
Eritrea’s flag is a rectangle divided into three triangles: a red isosceles triangle based on the hoist side, and a green upper and blue lower right triangle. A gold wreath encircling a gold olive branch is centred on the hoist side of the red triangle.— from the Ministry of Information government portal
 See also File:Flag of Eritrea Requirements.png.
The dimensions on this construction sheet match those shown at Flags of the World (FOTW) except that FOTW does not provide dimensions for the width or height of the wreath.

Testo del regio decreto 24 settembre 1923, n. 2072, come modificato dalla legge di conversione 24 dicembre 1925, n. 2264
Norme per l'uso della bandiera nazionale

Art. 1.
La bandiera nazionale, è formata da un drappo di forma rettangolare interzato in palo, di verde, di bianco e di rosso, col bianco coronato dallo stemma Reale bordato d'azzurro. Il drappo deve essere alto due terzi della sua lunghezza, e i tre colori vanno distribuiti nell'ordine anzidetto e in parti eguali, in guisa che il verde sia aderente all'inferitura. La bandiera di Stato, da usarsi nelle residenze dei Sovrani e della Reale Famiglia, nelle sedi del Parlamento, delle rappresentanze diplomatiche e consolari all'estero e degli uffici governativi, ha lo stemma sormontato dalla corona Reale.

Art. 2.
Per le bandiere nazionali usate dal Regio esercito, dalla Regia marina, dalla Regia aeronautica, come per quelle usate dalla marina mercantile e dagli Enti che ne ebbero disciplinato l'uso da apposite disposizioni, nulla è innovato alle prescrizioni ora vigenti.

Art. 3.
Le bandiere nazionali degli Enti pubblici locali hanno lo stemma senza corona, e con la bordatura azzurra.

Art. 4.
Gli Enti pubblici locali possono fare uso soltanto della bandiera nazionale e dei vessilli e gonfaloni tradizionali propri degli Enti, purché questi siano accompagnati alla bandiera nazionale, che avrà sempre il posto d'onore, a destra o in alto. L'autorità governativa può ordinare, secondo le consuetudini del Regno, che sui pubblici edifici delle Provincie, dei Comuni e degli Enti riconosciuti o vigilati dallo Stato sia esposta la bandiera nazionale. In caso di trasgressione, il Prefetto provvederà a termini di legge.

Art. 5.
In segno di lutto le bandiere degli edifici e quelle con sistemazione fissa devono essere tenute a mezz'asta; potranno anche avere due strisce di velo nero adattate all'estremità superiore dell'inferitura. Queste strisce sono obbligatorie invece per le bandiere che vengono portate nelle pubbliche cerimonie funebri.

Art. 6.
Nei festeggiamenti e nelle pubbliche funzioni la bandiera nazionale o di Stato deve avere la precedenza sopra tutti gli altri emblemi civili.

Art. 7.
Ferme rimanendo le norme e consuetudini di diritto internazionale per l'uso delle bandiere da parte delle rappresentanze diplomatiche e consolari estere, nessuno, cittadino o straniero, potrà nel Regno esporre bandiere di altri Stati, se non accompagnate alla bandiera italiana che occuperà sempre il posto d'onore, a destra, o in mezzo se le bandiere straniere sono più di una. In caso di trasgressione l'autorità di pubblica sicurezza provvederà alla immediata rimozione della o delle bandiere ed i colpevoli saranno puniti con multa da L. 1000 e 5000.

leaders.note: Reinado iniciado en1878 y continuado hasta1900; el soberano se distingue del presidente del Consejo. Los límites marcados como cobertura delimitan la ventana documental; no son nombramientos ni dimisiones.

leaders.name: Agostino Depretis
leaders.note: GabinetesVII yVIII, con renovación4/4/1887 sin cambio de presidente del Consejo.

leaders.name: Luigi Pelloux
leaders.note: Primer gabinete29/6/1898–14/5/1899 y segundo desde14/5/1899. El acta del Senado30/6/1898 reproduce el decreto de nombramiento29/6. Los límites marcados como cobertura delimitan la ventana documental; no son nombramientos ni dimisiones.

leaders.name: Umberto I
leaders.role: Rey de Italia · monarquía de Saboya
leaders.note: Asesinado en Monza29/7/1900. El comienzo de la ventana1900 no sustituye el acceso al trono de1878. Los límites marcados como cobertura delimitan la ventana documental; no son nombramientos ni dimisiones.

portrait.title: Fratelli Vianelli (Giuseppe e Luigi, flor. 1860-1890 ca) - VE - Umberto I di Savoia 1.jpg

leaders.name: Víctor Manuel III
leaders.role: Rey de Italia · monarquía de Saboya
leaders.note: Sucesor de UmbertoI; juramento parlamentario11/8/1900, distinto del comienzo sucesorio. El término continuó después de1919; no se añaden títulos imperiales adquiridos posteriormente. Los límites marcados como cobertura delimitan la ventana documental; no son nombramientos ni dimisiones.

leaders.note: Regresa en1887; sucesivas reelecciones hasta su asesinato26/7/1899. No equivale a un único mandato constitucional de doce años.

leaders.name: Juan Isidro Jimenes
leaders.note: Ventana interior de su primer mandato1899–1902, contrastada con mensajes originales al Congreso. El límite de marzo evita fingir resuelta la diferencia entre levantamiento, pérdida del poder y salida del país en abril/mayo1902. Los extremos marcados como cobertura no son nombramientos ni dimisiones.

leaders.name: Horacio Vásquez
leaders.note: Ventana interior del Gobierno provisional1902–1903; no fija el comienzo del levantamiento de abril ni el día de la sustitución por Woss y Gil. Los extremos marcados como cobertura no son nombramientos ni dimisiones.

leaders.name: Alejandro Woss y Gil
leaders.role: Presidente · Gobierno provisional y posterior fase constitucional
leaders.note: La relación naval contemporánea fecha la investidura constitucional20/6; otras cronologías distinguen elección e investidura de modo diferente. Se conserva una ventana interior anterior a su caída de noviembre, sin certificar todos los días del Gobierno provisional. Los extremos marcados como cobertura no son nombramientos ni dimisiones.

leaders.name: Carlos Felipe Morales Languasco
leaders.role: Presidente · Gobierno revolucionario y posterior fase constitucional
leaders.note: Circular original2/12/1903 comunica un Gobierno ya constituido. El extremo inicial es evidencia documental, no inicio de la revolución24/10 ni una investidura nacional ese día. La renuncia12/1/1906 se distingue de la pérdida práctica de autoridad en diciembre1905. Los extremos marcados como cobertura no son nombramientos ni dimisiones.

leaders.name: Eladio Victoria
leaders.note: La relación naval fecha la entrada6/12/1911 y renuncia26/11/1912. La elección de febrero1912 no se retrotrae a la entrada provisional.

leaders.name: Adolfo Alejandro Nouel
leaders.note: Investido1/12/1912. La ventana termina en febrero como cobertura: las fuentes distinguen anuncio de dimisión, aceptación y sustitución de marzo/abril1913; aquí no se fabrica una fecha final única. Los extremos marcados como cobertura no son nombramientos ni dimisiones.

leaders.name: Gobierno militar de Estados Unidos
leaders.note: La proclamación de ocupación29/11/1916 establece el Gobierno militar. No es una presidencia dominicana electa ni una anexión a Estados Unidos. La continuidad posterior se conserva en sus registros propios; no se inventa un retrato de este órgano. Los extremos marcados como cobertura no son nombramientos ni dimisiones.

leaders.name: Gobierno militar de Estados Unidos
leaders.note: Ventana documental de esta revisión: los extremos de cobertura no son nombramientos ni dimisiones. No constituye un censo de todas las suplencias del año. Órgano ocupante, no presidente dominicano ni retrato individual. La instalación del Gobierno provisional en1922 no puso fin a la ocupación, que continuó hasta1924.

leaders.name: Juan Bautista Vicini Burgos
leaders.note: Ventana documental de esta revisión: los extremos de cobertura no son nombramientos ni dimisiones. No constituye un censo de todas las suplencias del año. Investido21/10/1922; el límite1923 es cobertura de este hueco y no fin del Gobierno. El gobernador militar conservó facultades presupuestarias durante la transición.

leaders.role: Presidente de la República · jefatura formal del Estado
leaders.note: Ventana documental de esta revisión: los extremos de cobertura no son nombramientos ni dimisiones. No constituye un censo de todas las suplencias del año. leaders.name: Manuel de Jesús Troncoso de la Concha
leaders.role: Presidente de la República · jefatura formal del Estado
leaders.note: Ventana documental de esta revisión: los extremos de cobertura no son nombramientos ni dimisiones. No constituye un censo de todas las suplencias del año. El AGN documenta el paso de vicepresidente a presidente tras la muerte de Peynado y el periodo1940–1942; el inicio de año representa resolución anual y no una investidura el1deenero. El día del relevo requiere cotejo adicional y el cierre1941 no es cese.

leaders.name: Héctor Bienvenido Trujillo
leaders.role: Presidente de la República · jefatura formal del Estado
leaders.note: El Archivo General de la Nación acredita la presidencia1952–1960. Se conserva resolución anual y un límite documental en1959; no se afirma cese en ese año. Ventana documental de ejercicio: sus extremos delimitan cobertura, no nombramiento ni dimisión. Los relevos diarios no contrastados siguen pendientes.

leaders.role: Emir de Afganistán · Gobierno interno y tutela exterior británica
leaders.note: El museo fecha el ofrecimiento del trono en julio1880. La observación al cierre del mes no fija el día de acceso; el acuerdo restringe relaciones exteriores, sin convertir al emir en gobernador británico. Los extremos de cobertura delimitan la evidencia o la revisión; no son un nombramiento ni una dimisión.

leaders.name: Abdur Rahman Khan
leaders.role: Emir de Afganistán · autoridad interna bajo restricción exterior británica
leaders.note: Gobernante1880–1901. La biografía institucional de su sucesor fecha la designación de éste28/9/1901 y la muerte del padre tres días después. La influencia británica sobre las relaciones exteriores no suprime la jefatura afgana. Los límites de cobertura delimitan el tramo documentado por esta revisión, no un nombramiento o una dimisión.

leaders.name: Habibullah Khan

media.title: Flag of Cuba.svg
media.artist: Miguel Teurbe Tolón and Narciso López
media.credit:
Geometry and dimensions from Ley no 42 "de los Símbolos Nacionales".
Its shape is rectangular, twice length than width, composed by five horizontal stripes having all the same width, three deep blue and two white, placed alternating. A red equilateral triangle, in one of its vertical extremes occupy all the height of the flag constituting its fixed edge. Such triangle bears in its center a five-pointed white star, within an imaginary circumference, whose diameter is a third of the flag´s height, having one of its points towards the free upper edge of the flag.— English translation of Law 42 from Symbols of the Cuban Nation

leaders.name: Ranodip Singh Kunwar
leaders.role: Primer ministro de Nepal · Gobierno Rana
leaders.note: La oficina del primer ministro conserva su período en Bikram Sambat y la British Library identifica el mandato1877–1885. Límite anual observado, sin fingir cese el1de enero. Bir Shumsher tiene su serie posterior propia. Los extremos de cobertura delimitan esta observación o revisión; no representan un nombramiento ni un cese.

leaders.name: Surendra Bikram Shah
leaders.role: Rey de Nepal · autoridad real formal
leaders.note: La investigación de archivos diplomáticos sitúa el fallecimiento en mayo1881. Se observa hasta el cierre de ese mes, sin afirmar muerte el31. El Gobierno efectivo corresponde a los primeros ministros Rana. Los extremos de cobertura delimitan esta observación o revisión; no representan un nombramiento ni un cese.

leaders.name: Prithvi Bir Bikram Shah
leaders.role: Rey de Nepal · autoridad real formal
leaders.note: El archivo fotográfico de la British Library confirma reinado1881–1911; la investigación de SOAS sitúa la sucesión en mayo1881. El inicio normalizado al cierre del mes no es una fecha diaria de acceso; la coronación de diciembre es otro acto. Los extremos de cobertura delimitan esta observación o revisión; no representan un nombramiento ni un cese.

leaders.name: Bir Shumsher Jang Bahadur Rana
leaders.note: Ventana de adquisición1880–1899; los extremos de cobertura no son nombramientos ni dimisiones.

leaders.name: Bir Shumsher Jang Bahadur Rana
leaders.note: Ventana de adquisición1900–1919; los extremos de cobertura no son nombramientos ni dimisiones.

leaders.name: Prithvi Bir Bikram Shah
leaders.role: Rey de Nepal · jefatura formal bajo el Gobierno Rana
leaders.note: La inscripción original de su estatua transcrita por el Departamento de Arqueología fecha la muerte11/12/1911. La monarquía formal se distingue del poder gubernamental Rana. Los límites de cobertura delimitan el tramo documentado por esta revisión, no un nombramiento o una dimisión.

leaders.name: Dev Shumsher Jung Bahadur Rana
leaders.role: Primer ministro Rana · ejercicio efectivo del Gobierno
leaders.note: Ventana interior de ejercicio documentado. Los repertorios discrepan entre marzo y mayo para el inicio; esta ficha no convierte15/5 en fecha contrastada de nombramiento. Chandra lo sustituye en junio. Los límites de cobertura delimitan el tramo documentado por esta revisión, no un nombramiento o una dimisión.

leaders.note: Documenta Nepalica registra el mandato27/6/1901–26/11/1929. Se conserva el mandato posterior a1919 y no se atribuye a Chandra el título de rey. Los límites de cobertura delimitan el tramo documentado por esta revisión, no un nombramiento o una dimisión.

leaders.note: Reinado1911–1955. La ventana al cierre1911 no pretende fechar su acceso ni coronación. Los límites de cobertura delimitan el tramo documentado por esta revisión, no un nombramiento o una dimisión.

media.title: Flag of Niger.svg
media.artist: Made by: Philippe Verdy User:verdy_p, see also fr:Utilisateur:verdy_p.
media.credit:
The flag of Niger often has the unusual 7:6 proportions. The three bands have exactly the same size. For exact and complete coverage of the image, it is used as background. The central filled circle is at least 50% of the median band in diameter. 85% is used for better rendering at small sizes. For reference colors, see Flags of the world that define Pantone colors. For Pantone color conversion, please use ONLY the sRGB color profile (at reference gamma = 2.2 on CRT screen, without gamma correction by software or by the graphics display driver, as defined in IEC 61966-2.1, and with slope limit of 1/32, this limit affecting only the indices 1 to 14 in the 8-bit colorimetric component space 0 to 255):
The "burnt orange" color in the top band and circle is Pantone(166), i.e. RGB(224,82,6) = #E05206 on sRGB CRT screen, or CMYK(0,65%,100%,0) for process coated print, BUT NOT light orange #FF7000 which is somewhere between Pantone(130C) and Pantone(151), and is even lighter than X11 orange! See https://web.archive.org/web/20060207090052/http://www.seoconsultants.com/css/colors/conversion/100/ 
The central white band is plain D65 reference white = RGB(255,255,255) = #FFFFFF. 

The green color in the bottom band is Pantone(361), i.e. RGB(13,176,43) = #0DB02B on sRGB CRT screen, or CMYK(76%,0,91%,0) for process coated print, BUT NOT grass green #36A100 which too burnt and more like Pantone(369)! See https://web.archive.org/web/20060207090040/https://www.seoconsultants.com/css/colors/conversion/300/

leaders.role: Miembro del triunvirato boer · Gobierno restaurado disputado
leaders.note: Proclamación de restauración13/12/1880 tras ocupación británica de1877. Comparte el poder conJoubert yPretorius; no es aún presidente electo individual ni supone control boer uniforme durante la guerra. Las leyes de1882 identifican al triunvirato y aKruger como vicepresidente.

leaders.name: Paul Kruger
leaders.role: Presidente de la República Sudafricana · Transvaal
leaders.note: Elegido16/4/1883, juramento9/5/1883. Las reelecciones posteriores renuevan el mandato sin cambiar la identidad personal; se acota esta serie a1899 conservando literalmente los registros de1900 en adelante. Los extremos de cobertura delimitan esta observación o revisión; no representan un nombramiento ni un cese.

leaders.name: Paul Kruger
leaders.role: Presidente de la República Sudafricana · después representante en el exilio
leaders.note: Sus memorias reproducen la decisión del Consejo Ejecutivo10/9/1900: licencia para Europa y sustitución por el vicepresidenteBurger. Desde entonces no se le atribuye dirección presencial ni control de toda la república; las proclamaciones de anexión británicas y la resistencia coexistieron hasta la paz. Los límites marcados como cobertura delimitan la ventana documental; no son nombramientos ni dimisiones.

leaders.name: Schalk Willem Burger
leaders.role: Vicepresidente y presidente interino · Gobierno bóer en campaña
leaders.note: Decisión10/9 reproducida en las memorias deKruger; Ditsong fecha la partida física11/9. Es sustitución en el ejercicio, no dos presidentes con idéntico poder ni territorio bajo control íntegro. El tratado deVereeniging31/5/1902 pone fin a la resistencia gubernamental.

leaders.name: Eduardo VII
leaders.role: Soberano británico · autoridad externa de la colonia
leaders.note: Vereeniging31/5/1902 reconoce la soberanía británica. La colonia continúa hasta la Unión de1910; la ventana cierra1909 por el ámbito de estos polígonos anuales, no por muerte ni fin del reinado. Los frentes militares1900–1902 no se reconstruyen a partir de este registro. Los límites marcados como cobertura delimitan la ventana documental; no son nombramientos ni dimisiones.

media.title: Flag of the Kingdom of Württemberg (1806 - 1816).png
media.credit:
Own work - 
Below is a list with written sources referring to this flag
Swabisches Chronik, 5th of August 1803 - "[...] wurde oben in der Residenz die dreifarbige Württembergische fahnen aufgezogen." 
(The tricolor Württemberg flag was raised at the top of the residence.)
Matthison, Friedrich von. Das Dianenfest bei Bebenhausen. 1813 - "Schauf auf der Emichsburg ihr hoch, Die Königsflagge wehn? [...]" 
(Look up at the Emichsburg, the royal flag is flying?)
Memminger, Johann Daniel Georg von. Stuttgart und Ludwigsburg, mit ihrer Umgebung, Germany: Stuttgart, 1817. - "Auf dem Alten Schlosse weht eine große dreyfarbige fahne, die aber, wenn König sich aud der Residenz enrfernt, eingezogen wird und betzwegen zum zeichen seiner abwesenheit dient." (On the Old Castle flies a large tricolor flag, which, however, is taken down when the King leaves the residence and serves as a symbol of his absence.)
In reference to the Emichsburg: 
[...] die staatliche fahne die während der anwesenheit des Königs auf ihrem thurme weht, [...] (the state flag that flies on its tower during the presence of the King.)
Unknown author, Watercolor of Stuttgart, 1815. -  
Eine Fähne welche aufgestecht wird sobald Ihre Majestät in der Stadt sind.
[...] die flagge zeigt die Kgl. Farben unter König friedrich. (A flag that is raised as soon as His Majesty is in town. [...] The flag shows the royal colors under King Frederick)
Many contemporary depictions show the flags mentioned in these excerpts, most famously, a painting by Johann Baptist Seele.
The usage of the words Staatliche (stately) most possibly indicates that the colors were used as the "Landesfarben" (national colors) of the country, something that can be confirmed in the following excerpt:
Starklof, Richard. Geschichte des kgl. württembergischen zweiten Reiter-Regiments, ehemaligen Jäger-Regiments zu Pferde Herzog Louis, Germany:Eduard Zernin, 1862. - 

Seit Beginn des Jahres 1810 trugen die württembergischen Truppen (durch allerh. Ordre vom 1 Januar) auf der linken Seite des Huts , Kaskets , der Bärenmüze u. s. w. unten am Federbusch in einer schwarz-roth-gelben Kokarde die württembergischen Landesfarben.  (Since the beginning of 1810, the Württemberg troops wore (by order of 1 January) on the left side of the hat, Casquet, Bearskin etc. at the bottom of the plume in a black, red and yellow cockade the Württemberg national colours.)

https://imagesonline.bl.uk/asset/143693.
Per page x of the The Contest for Rule in Eighteenth-Century Iran: Idea of Iran Vol. 11, the artist is unknown, and the work was created in circa 1740.
British Library:[1]
Source: Foster 44

Caption: Nadir Shah of Persia (1732-1747). Three-quarter length, in an oval cartouche. The Shah wears a scarlet tunic with a sleeveless outer garment trimmed with fur. On his head is a high cap (a ‘tahmazi’) ornamented with a jewelled aigrette. The face is turned a little to the right. The left hand rests on the hip, the right holds a string of pearls. Jewelled bracelets on his upper arms.

media.title: Saadi flag.svg
media.credit:
Own work based on:
Marinid:

O'Callaghan, Joseph F. (17 March 2011)    (in English)   The Gibraltar Crusade: Castile and the Battle for the Strait, University of Pennsylvania Press, pp. 185  ISBN:  978-0-8122-0463-6. : Spanish Historian and Arabist Ambrosio Huici Miranda suggested that the Marinids used white banners, much like their Almohad predecessors.
Abitbol, Michel (10 April 2014)    (in French)   Histoire du Maroc, Place des éditeurs, pp. 126  ISBN:  978-2-262-03816-8. : When the morning light shines, the Sultan mounts his horse and the white standard which is the flag of the dynasty, called al-Mansur (the Victorious) is carried next to him. Immediately before him march the armed men on foot; the horses held in hand, covered with caparisons of patterned cloth, that is to say, saddle blankets.

Bennison, Amira K. (2014) "Drums, Banners and Baraka: Symbols of authority during the first century of Marīnid rule, 1250-1350" in Bennison, Amira K., ed. (in English)   The Articulation of Power in Medieval Iberia and the Maghrib, Oxford University Press, pp. 194–216  : "The naming of the Marinid palatine city, Madīnat al-Bayḍā', the White City, reflects their use of white as a dynastic colour."
عاصم, محمد رزق (2006)    (in arabic)   رايات الإسلام من اللواء النبوي الأبيض إلى العلم العثماني الأحمر, Cairo:  مكتبة مدبولي, pp. 151   : Egyptian historiographer Al-Qalqashandi (d. 1418) recalled a white flag made of silk with verses from the Qur’an written in gold at the top of the circle as the sultanate’s emblem among the kings of the Banu Abd al-Haqq of the Banu Marin in Morocco, calling it the Victorious Flag.
عاصم, محمد رزق (2006)    (in arabic)   رايات الإسلام من اللواء النبوي الأبيض إلى العلم العثماني الأحمر, Cairo:  مكتبة مدبولي, pp. 151  : Maghrebi historian Ibn Khaldun talked about the flags he saw during the time of Sultan Abu al-Hasan, indicating that they used to give governors, workers, and commanders permission to take one small flag made of white linen.
Julien, Charles André; Internet Archive (1970)       History of North Africa: Tunisia, Algeria, Morocco. From the Arab Conquest to 1830, New York, Praeger, pp. 198  ISBN:  978-0-7100-6614-5. : Contemporary historian Charles-André Julien references the small white flag as a miniature version of the royal standard that was given to the main commander on the battlefield as a mark of authority to lead the troops. The flag was raised in conquered fortresses.
Markham, Clements R. (Clements Robert); Kelly - University of Toronto (1912)       Book of knowledge of all the kingdoms, lands, and lordships that are in the world, and the arms and devices of each land and lordship, or of the kings and lords who possess them, London, The Hakluyt society, pp. 26  : The Book of Knowledge of All Kingdoms, written by a Franciscan friar in the 14th century, describes the flag of Fez, the Marinid capital, as being plain white.
Saadian:

III, Comer Plummer (2015)    (in English)   Roads to Ruin: The War for Morocco in the Sixteenth Century, Lulu.com, pp. 26  ISBN:  978-1-4834-3105-5. : "It was unconventional to be sure, as was the Saadian standard, a dramatic statement in white, richly embroidered in golden Qur'anic verses. The white standard was an old Merinid tradition bestowed by the sultan upon faithful commanders. But, as a king in his own right, and in eschewing the familiar green of Islam, Mohammad ash-Shaykh made it look so very new."
Smith, Whitney; Internet Archive (1975)    (in English)   Flags through the ages and across the world, McGraw-Hill, pp. 254  ISBN:  978-0-07-059093-9. : "From the eleventh century until the beginning of the seventeenth, the principal color was white under the Almoravids, Marinids, and Saadians."
Abitbol, Michel (2014)    (in French)   Histoire du Maroc, Éditions Perrin  DOI:  10.3917/perri.abitb.2014.01. ISBN:  978-2-262-03816-8. :"al-Ifrani, who also notes the presence of many valuable horses in these parades, as well as standards of several colors including the white banner of the sultan [Ahmed al-Mansour]" Check: al-Ifrānī, Muḥammad as-Suġaiyir (1888)    (in Arabic)   Nuzhat al-ḥādī bi-aḫbār mulūk al-qarn al-ḥādī: Nozhet-elhâdi, histoire de la dynastie Saadienne au Maroc (1511 - 1670), Leroux, pp. 117  .
Palomares, Lucien (11 July 2012)    (in French)   Tarik es Salama, Lulu.com, pp. 266  ISBN:  978-1-4717-8163-6.  :"Les dynasties précédentes,  Mérinides et Saadiens, utilisaient le drapeau blanc."
العزيز, بنعبد الله، عبد (1957)    (in Arabic)   مظاهر الحضارة المغربية, دار السلمى،, pp. 43  : "As for the flag, it was white at the beginning of the Islamic era, by analogy with the flag of the Fatimids and Umayyads (unlike the Abbasid flag, which was black and then blue. The flag of the princes of Sanhaja was multi-colored, but it became white in the days of the Almohads, Marinids, and Saadians. Then the Alawites chose red."

portrait.title: Jalal al-Din Khwarazmshah confronts Chinggis Khan across the Indus. Rashid al-Din, Jami‘ al-tawarikh, National Library of Russia, St Petersburg, MS. Dorn 289, fols. 125v–126r (Jalal al-Din Khwarazmshah with weapons).jpg
portrait.credit:
The Illustration of History in Persian Manuscripts Figure 3

"A later copy of the Jami‘ al-tawarikh, produced in Turusht [which was near the town of Rayy (near present-day Tehran)] in 935/1529 and now in St Petersburg from the library of the shrine at Ardabil, contains 29 paintings, including the exploit of Jalal al-Din Khwarazmshah crossing the Indus (Figure 3).57 This is a double-page painting (the only one in this manuscript), showing the sultan on the left-hand page, not looking at all like someone who has just plunged across the Indus, but standing with his beautifully caparisoned horse and wiping his sword dry with a blue cloth. It reflects the text to the extent that he still has his shield over his shoulder and has planted his banner defiantly on the bank. Perhaps more interesting is the right-hand side of the painting, which shows Chinggis Khan turning back towards his sons and entourage, remarking on Jalal al-Din’s valour." The Illustration of History in Persian Manuscripts page 10
